before.name: revcl-AppropriateDataCollectionMonitoringRequirements
before.title: Ensure that monitoring requirements have been assessed and that appropriate data collection and alerting configurations are applied

before.name: revcl-AutomatedBackupVAzureVms
before.title: Review the use of Automated Backup v2 for Azure VMs.

before.name: revcl-AvailabilityZoneZoneDeployment
before.title: If deploying to an availability zone, ensure that the VM's zone deployment is available once the quota has been approved. Submit a support request with the subscription, VM series, number of CPUs and availability zone required.

before.name: revcl-AzureBestPracticesAzureInfrastructure
before.title: Perform a quality check for SAP HANA on the provisioned Azure infrastructure to verify that provisioned VMs comply with SAP HANA on Azure best practices.

before.name: revcl-AzureBlobStorageSqlServer
before.title: Review the use of Azure Blob Storage with SQL Server 2016.

before.name: revcl-AzureDiagnosticExtensionLogStorageSharedStorageAccounts
before.title: When necessary, use shared storage accounts within the landing zone for Azure diagnostic extension log storage.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorDeliveryApplicationContent
before.title: Develop a plan for securing the delivery application content from your Workload spokes using Application Gateway and Azure Front door.  You can use the Application Delivery checklist to for recommendations.

before.name: revcl-AzureLandingZoneArchitectureLeverageDeclarativeInfrastructure
before.title: Leverage Declarative Infrastructure as Code Tools such as Azure Bicep, ARM Templates or Terraform to build and maintain your Azure Landing Zone architecture. Both from a Platform and Application workload perspective.

before.name: revcl-AzureLandingZonePlatformTeamFunctions
before.title: Aim to define functions for Azure Landing Zone Platform team.

before.name: revcl-AzureLinuxVmBackupStrategiesOracleDatabase
before.title: Review Oracle Database in Azure Linux VM backup strategies.

before.name: revcl-AzureNativeIdentityServicesManagedServiceProviders
before.title: If you partner with customers by managing their SAP estates, consider Azure Lighthouse. Azure Lighthouse allows managed service providers to use Azure native identity services to authenticate to the customers' environment. It puts the control in the hands of customers, because they can revoke access at any time and audit service providers' actions.

before.name: revcl-AzureNetworkWatcherNetworkLatencyMeasurements
before.title: Use Connection Monitor in Azure Network Watcher to monitor latency metrics for SAP databases and application servers. Or collect and display network latency measurements by using Azure Monitor.

before.name: revcl-AzureRoleAssignmentsDenyPolicies
before.title: Use deny policies to supplement Azure role assignments. The combination of deny policies and Azure role assignments ensures the appropriate guardrails are in place to enforce who can deploy and configure resources and what resources they can deploy and configure.

before.name: revcl-AzureServiceHealthPlatformActionGroups
before.title: Include alerts and action groups as part of the Azure Service Health platform to ensure that alerts or issues can be actioned

before.name: revcl-AzureSiteRecoveryMonitoringDisasterRecoveryService-1
before.title: Use Azure Site Recovery monitoring to maintain the health of the disaster recovery service for SAP application servers.

before.name: revcl-AzureTaggingResources
before.title: Azure tagging can be leveraged to logically group and track resources, automate their deployments, and most importantly, provide visibility on the incurred costs.

before.name: revcl-AzureUpdateManagerAvailableUpdates
before.title: Use Azure Update Manager to check the status of available updates for a single VM or multiple VMs and consider scheduling regular patching.

before.name: revcl-BranchingStrategyVersionControl
before.title: Follow a branching strategy to allow teams to collaborate better and efficiently manage version control of IaC and application Code. Review options such as Github Flow.

before.name: revcl-CiCdPipelineIacArtifacts
before.title: Use a CI/CD pipeline to deploy IaC artifacts and ensure the quality of your deployment and Azure environments.

before.name: revcl-CombinedProcessInnovationProcess
before.title: Integrate security into the already combined process of development and operations in DevOps to mitigate risks in the innovation process.

before.name: revcl-CriticalSharedServicesResourceLocks
before.title: Use resource locks to prevent accidental deletion of critical shared services.

before.name: revcl-CrossFunctionalDevopsPlatformTeamAzureLandingZoneArchitecture
before.title: Ensure you have a cross functional DevOps Platform Team to build, manage and maintain your Azure Landing Zone architecture.

before.name: revcl-DevopsPlatformTeamSupportApplicationWorkloadTeams
before.title: Aim to define functions for application workload teams to be self-sufficient and not require DevOps Platform Team support. Achieve this through the use of custom RBAC role.

before.name: revcl-DifferentDnsZonesPrivateDnsZones
before.title: Use different DNS zones to distinguish each environment (sandbox, development, preproduction, and production) from each other. The exception is for SAP deployments with their own VNet; here, private DNS zones might not be necessary.

before.name: revcl-EnablingWriteAcceleratorMSeries
before.title: Enabling Write accelerator for M series when using premium disks(V1)

before.name: revcl-ExistingAzureBasedSapSystemsSapSolutions
before.title: Azure Center for SAP solutions (ACSS) is an Azure offering that makes SAP a top-level workload on Azure. ACSS is an end-to-end solution that enables you to create and run SAP systems as a unified workload on Azure and provides a more seamless foundation for innovation. You can take advantage of the management capabilities for both new and existing Azure-based SAP systems.

before.name: revcl-ExistingManagementGroupPoliciesSapSubscriptions
before.title: enforce existing Management Group policies to SAP Subscriptions

before.name: revcl-FastViolationDetectionConsistentPolicyAdherence
before.title: Use Azure Policy for access control and compliance reporting. Azure Policy provides the ability to enforce organization-wide settings to ensure consistent policy adherence and fast violation detection.

before.name: revcl-GlobalTransitConnectivityGlobalNetworks
before.title: Use Virtual WAN for Azure deployments in new, large, or global networks where you need global transit connectivity across Azure regions and on-premises locations. With this approach, you won't need to manually set up transitive routing for Azure networking, and you can follow a standard for SAP on Azure deployments.

before.name: revcl-HighAvailabilitySuseClustersSapSolutionManager
before.title: Use Azure Monitor for SAP solutions to monitor your SAP workloads(SAP HANA, high-availability SUSE clusters, and SQL systems) on Azure. Consider supplementing Azure Monitor for SAP solutions with SAP Solution Manager.

before.name: revcl-IpAddressDrSide
before.title: Consider reserving IP address on DR side when configuring ASR

before.name: revcl-LeverageAzureResourceTagResourceGrouping
before.title: Leverage Azure resource tag for cost categorization and resource grouping (: BillTo, Department (or Business Unit), Environment (Production, Stage, Development), Tier (Web Tier, Application Tier), Application Owner, ProjectName)

before.name: revcl-ManySystemInterfacesSapLandscape
before.title: If the virtual machine's DNS or virtual name is not changed during migration to Azure, Background DNS and virtual names connect many system interfaces in the SAP landscape, and customers are only sometimes aware of the interfaces that developers define over time. Connection challenges arise between various systems when virtual or DNS names change after migrations, and it's recommended to retain DNS aliases to prevent these types of difficulties.

before.name: revcl-MaximumNetworkThroughputSapLandingZones
before.title: Virtual WAN manages connectivity between spoke VNets for virtual-WAN-based topologies (no need to set up user-defined routing [UDR] or NVAs), and maximum network throughput for VNet-to-VNet traffic in the same virtual hub is 50 gigabits per second. If necessary, SAP landing zones can use VNet peering to connect to other landing zones and overcome this bandwidth limitation.

before.name: revcl-MultipleDelegatedSubnetsOneDelegatedSubnet
before.title: While Azure does help you to create multiple delegated subnets in a VNet, only one delegated subnet can exist in a VNet for Azure NetApp Files. Attempts to create a new volume will fail if you use more than one delegated subnet for Azure NetApp Files.

before.name: revcl-NativePaasServiceDisasterRecoveryCapabilities
before.title: Ensure to use and test native PaaS service disaster recovery capabilities.

before.name: revcl-NetworkVirtualAppliancesPartnerNetworkingTechnologies
before.title: Consider deploying network virtual appliances (NVAs) between regions only if partner NVAs are used. NVAs between regions or VNets aren't required if native NVAs are present. When you're deploying partner networking technologies and NVAs, follow the vendor's guidance to verify conflicting configurations with Azure networking.

before.name: revcl-NewLandingZoneSubscriptionVending
before.title: Implement automation for new landing zone for applications and workloads through subscription vending

before.name: revcl-OverallPlatformMonitoringSolutionResourceHealthEvents
before.title: Include service and resource health events as part of the overall platform monitoring solution. Tracking service and resource health from the platform perspective is an important component of resource management in Azure.

before.name: revcl-OverlappingIpAddressRangesDrSites-1
before.title: Avoid using overlapping IP address ranges for production and DR sites.

before.name: revcl-PlatformComponentsLandingZone
before.title: Establish monitoring for platform components of your landing zone, AMBA is a framework solution that is available and provides an easy way to scale alerting by using Azure Policy

before.name: revcl-PullRequestStrategyCodeChanges
before.title: Adopt a pull request strategy to help keep control of code changes merged into branches.

before.name: revcl-QuickFixesTechnicalDebt
before.title: Establish a process for using code to implement quick fixes. Always register quick fixes in your team's backlog so each fix can be reworked at a later point, and you can limit technical debt.

before.name: revcl-RawLogEntriesPremisesMonitoringSystems
before.title: Don't send raw log entries back to on-premises monitoring systems. Instead, adopt a principle that data born in Azure stays in Azure. If on-premises SIEM integration is required, then send critical alerts instead of logs.

before.name: revcl-RequiredServicesDeploymentRegions
before.title: Ensure required services and features are available within the chosen deployment regions eg. ANF , Zone etc.

before.name: revcl-SameSapSubscriptionAdditionalRouting
before.title: Integrate tightly coupled applications into the same SAP subscription to avoid additional routing and management complexity

before.name: revcl-SapBasisOperationsSapLandscapeManagement
before.title: Optimize and manage SAP Basis operations by using SAP Landscape Management (LaMa). Use the SAP LaMa connector for Azure to relocate, copy, clone, and refresh SAP systems.

before.name: revcl-SapDeploymentAutomationFrameworkOpenSourceOrchestrationTool
before.title: Azure supports automating SAP deployments in Linux and Windows. SAP Deployment Automation Framework is an open-source orchestration tool that can deploy, install, and maintain SAP environments.

before.name: revcl-SapHanaSystemLandscapeGuidance
before.title: Review the Monitoring the SAP HANA System Landscape guidance.

before.name: revcl-ScaleUnitLeverageSubscription
before.title: Leverage Subscription as scale unit and scaling our resources, consider deploying subscription per environment eg. Sandbox, non-prod, prod

before.name: revcl-TimeZoneMatchesOperatingSystem

before.name: revcl-TotalAvailableVmCoresQuotaIncrease

before.name: revcl-UnderlyingAzureExtensionVmExtension
before.title: Run a VM Extension for SAP check. VM Extension for SAP uses the assigned managed identity of a virtual machine (VM) to access VM monitoring and configuration data. The check ensures that all performance metrics in your SAP application come from the underlying Azure Extension for SAP.

before.name: revcl-UnitTestsApplicationCode

before.name: revcl-VersionControlSystemSourceCode

before.name: revcl-PowershellAutomationScriptsManagement

before.title: Use Backends feature to eliminate redundant API backend configurations

before.name: revcl-AzureVmwareSolutionVirtualMachineConnectionMonitor

before.title: Use Azure Policy to onboard Azure VMware Solution workloads in the Azure Management, Monitoring and Security solutions

before.name: revcl-CoreAzureVmwareSolutionMonitoringInsightsDashboards
before.title: Create dashboards to enable core Azure VMware Solution monitoring insights

before.name: revcl-DiskPoolBackedDatastoreDataRepositories
before.title: Ensure data repositories for the backup solution are stored outside of vSAN storage. Either in Azure native or on a disk pool-backed datastore

before.name: revcl-EsxiHostDensityLeadTime
before.title: Ensure that you have a policy around ESXi host density and efficiency, keeping in mind the lead time for requesting new nodes

before.name: revcl-ExistingUpdateManagementToolingAzureUpdateManagement
before.title: Include workloads running on Azure VMware Solution in existing update management tooling or in Azure Update Management

before.name: revcl-HumanUnderstandableNamesExrAuthorizationKeys
before.title: Implement human understandable names for ExR authorization keys to allow for easy identification of the keys purpose/use

before.name: revcl-ManualDeploymentsConfiguration
before.title: For manual deployments, all configuration and deployments must be documented

before.name: revcl-MinimalPrivateCloudAutomatedDeployments
before.title: For automated deployments, deploy a minimal private cloud and scale as needed

before.name: revcl-RdPartySolutionsAccessConstraints
before.title: Ensure that access constraints to ESXi are understood, there are access limits which might affect 3rd party solutions.

before.name: revcl-RelevantResourceLocksAutomatedDeployment
before.title: For automated deployment, ensure that relevant resource locks are created through the automation or through Azure Policy for proper governance

before.name: revcl-RouteServerExrGateway
before.title: When route server is used, ensure no more then 1000 routes are propagated from route server to ExR gateway to on-premises (ARS limit).

before.name: revcl-SeparateServicePrinciplesAzureVmwareSolution
before.title: Use Key vault to store secrets and authorization keys when separate Service Principles are used for deploying Azure VMware Solution and ExpressRoute

before.name: revcl-SingleTierGatewayAzurePortalApis
before.title: When performing automated configuration of NSX-T segments with a single Tier-1 gateway, use Azure Portal APIs instead of NSX-Manager APIs

before.name: revcl-VpnConnectionsConnectionMonitor
before.title: Ensure ExpressRoute or VPN connections from on-premises to Azure are monitored using 'connection monitor'

before.name: revcl-VrealizeNetworkInsightsVrealizeOperations
before.title: If deep insight in VMware vSphere is required: Is vRealize Operations and/or vRealize Network Insights used in the solution?

before.name: revcl-VsanStoragePolicyDefaultStoragePolicy
before.title: Ensure the vSAN storage policy for VM's is NOT the default storage policy as this policy applies thick provisioning

before.name: revcl-VsphereContentLibrariesFiniteResource
before.title: Ensure vSphere content libraries are not placed on vSAN as vSAN is a finite resource

before.name: wafsg-AppropriateMetricsObservability
before.title: Observability: Monitor, aggregate, and visualize appropriate metrics.

before.name: wafsg-AutomatedKeyRotationStrategyKeyBasedAuthentication
before.title: Automate for efficiency: If you use key-based authentication, implement an automated key-rotation strategy.

before.name: wafsg-AzureApiManagementAzureOpenaiDiagnostics
before.title: Observability: If Azure OpenAI diagnostics are insufficient for your needs, consider using a gateway like Azure API Management in front of Azure OpenAI to log both incoming prompts and outgoing responses where permitted. This information can help you understand the effectiveness of the model for incoming prompts.

before.name: wafsg-AzureDevopsCultureAzureOpenaiInstances
before.title: Azure DevOps culture: Ensure deployment of Azure OpenAI instances across your various environments, such as development, test, and production. Ensure that you have environments to support continuous learning and experimentation throughout the development cycle.

before.name: wafsg-AzureOpenaiModelDeployments
before.title: Deploy with confidence: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to deploy Azure OpenAI, model deployments, and other infrastructure required for fine-tuning models.

before.name: wafsg-AzureOpenaiServiceAzureDiagnostics
before.title: Enable and configure Azure Diagnostics: Enable and configure Diagnostics for the Azure OpenAI Service.
before.description: Diagnostics collects and analyzes metrics and logs, helping you monitor the availability, performance, and operation of Azure OpenAI.

before.name: wafsg-LargeLanguageModelOperationsAzureOpenaiLlms
before.title: Deploy with confidence: Follow large language model operations (LLMOps) practices to operationalize the management of your Azure OpenAI LLMs, including deployment, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering.

before.name: revcl-AzureAutomanageMachineConfigurationAuditCapabilitiesOsLevelVirtualMachine
before.title: Monitor OS level virtual machine (VM) configuration drift using Azure Policy. Enabling Azure Automanage Machine Configuration audit capabilities through policy helps application team workloads to immediately consume feature capabilities with little effort.

before.name: revcl-AzureUpdateManagerPatchingMechanism-1
before.title: Use Azure Update Manager as a patching mechanism for Windows and Linux VMs outside of Azure using Azure Arc.

before.name: revcl-AzureUpdateManagerPatchingMechanism
before.title: Use Azure Update Manager as a patching mechanism for Windows and Linux VMs in Azure.

before.name: revcl-AzureVirtualMachinesDisasterRecoveryScenariosAzureSiteRecovery
before.title: Use Azure Site Recovery for Azure-to-Azure Virtual Machines disaster recovery scenarios. This enables you to replicate workloads across regions.

before.name: wafsg-AutomaticVmGuestPatchingLinuxVirtualMachines
before.title: Have processes for installing automatic updates. Consider using Automatic VM guest patching for a timely rollout of critical patches and security patches. Use Azure Update Manager to manage OS updates for your Windows and Linux virtual machines in Azure.

before.name: wafsg-AzureChaosStudioFaultLibrariesTestEnvironment
before.title: Build a test environment that closely matches your production environment to test updates and changes before you deploy them to production. Have processes in place to test the security updates, performance baselines, and reliability faults. Take advantage of Azure Chaos Studio fault libraries to inject and simulate error conditions. For more information, see Azure Chaos Studio fault and action library.

before.name: wafsg-AzureComputeGalleryScaleSet
before.title: (VMs, scale set) Automatically deploy VM applications from the Azure Compute Gallery by defining the applications in the profile.
before.description: The VMs in the scale set are created and the specified apps are preinstalled, which makes management easier.

before.name: wafsg-AzureMonitorAlertsResourceUsage
before.title: Monitor the VM instances. Collect logs and metrics from VM instances to monitor resource usage and measure the health of the instances. Some common metrics include CPU usage, number of requests, and input/output (I/O) latency. Set up Azure Monitor alerts to be notified about issues and to detect configuration changes in your environment.

before.name: wafsg-AzureUpdateManagerScaleSet
before.title: (Scale set) Keep your VMs up to date by setting an upgrade policy. We recommend rolling upgrades. However, if you need granular control, choose to upgrade manually.  For Flexible orchestration, you can use  Azure Update Manager.
before.description: Security is the primary reason for upgrades. Security assurances for the instances shouldn't decay over time.  Rolling upgrades are done in batches, which ensures all instances aren't down at the same time.

before.name: wafsg-FollowingOptionsCustomScripts
before.title: Automate processes for bootstrapping, running scripts, and configuring VMs. You can automate processes by using extensions or custom scripts. We recommend the following options:

before.name: wafsg-HealthVms
before.title: Monitor the health of the VMs and their dependencies.

before.name: wafsg-OsSpecificDataCollectionRulesMonitorAgentExtension
before.title: (VMs, scale set) Monitor and measure the health of the VM instances.  Deploy the Monitor agent extension to your VMs to collect monitoring data from the guest OS with OS-specific data collection rules.  Enable VM insights to monitor health and performance and to view trends from the collected data. Use boot diagnostics to get information as VMs boot. Boot diagnostics also diagnose boot failures.
before.description: Monitoring data is at the core of incident resolution. A comprehensive monitoring stack provides information about how the VMs are performing and their health. By continuously monitoring the instances, you can be ready for or prevent failures like performance overload and reliability issues.

before.name: wafsg-PrebuiltSoftwareComponentsSoftwareInstallation
before.title: Install prebuilt software components as extensions as part of bootstrapping.  Azure supports many extensions that can be used to configure, monitor, secure, and provide utility applications for your VMs.   Enable automatic upgrades on extensions.
before.description: Extensions can help simplify the software installation at scale without you having to manually install, configure, or upgrade it on each VM.

before.name: wafsg-QuotaLevel
before.title: Manage your quota. Plan what level of quota your workload requires and review that level regularly as the workload evolves. If you need to increase or decrease your quota, request those changes early.

before.name: wafsg-RegularSystemPatchingImmediatePatchApplication
before.title: Create a maintenance plan that includes regular system patching as a part of routine operations. Include emergency processes that allow for immediate patch application. You can have custom processes to manage patching or partially delegate the task to Azure.

before.name: wafsg-VirtualMachineScaleSetsMultipleFaultDomains
before.title: (Scale set) Virtual Machine Scale Sets in Flexible orchestration mode can help simplify the deployment and management of your workload. For example, you can easily manage self-healing by using automatic repairs.
before.description: Flexible orchestration can manage VM instances at scale. Handing individual VMs adds operational overhead.  For example, when you delete VM instances, the associated disks and NICs are also automatically deleted. VM instances are spread across multiple fault domains so that update operations don't disrupt service.

before.name: wafsg-AksBestPracticesDocumentationWorkloadArchitectures
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Review AKS best practices documentation.
before.description: To build and run applications successfully in AKS, there are key considerations to understand and implement. These areas include multi-tenancy and scheduler features, cluster, and pod security, or business continuity and disaster recovery.

before.name: wafsg-AutomatedDeploymentProcessesSoftwareDevelopmentLifecycle
before.title: Workload architecture: Use a repeatable and automated deployment processes for your workload within your software development lifecycle.

before.name: wafsg-AzureChaosStudioDisasterRecoverySituations
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Review Azure Chaos Studio.
before.description: Azure Chaos Studio can help simulate faults and trigger disaster recovery situations.

before.name: wafsg-CentralizedConsistentMannerPodsConfigurationStandards
before.title: Cluster architecture: Operationalize clusters and pods configuration standards with Azure Policy.
before.description: Azure Policy can help to apply at-scale enforcement and safeguards on your clusters in a centralized, consistent manner. It can also control what functions pods are granted and if anything is running against company policy.

before.name: wafsg-ChaosEngineeringPracticesPlatformReliabilityIssues
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Use chaos engineering practices that target Kubernetes to identify application or platform reliability issues.

before.name: wafsg-CoreApiServerInteractionsClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Enable diagnostics settings to ensure control plane or core API server interactions are logged.

before.name: wafsg-DifferentAzureRegionsInternetFacingWorkloads-1
before.title: Cluster architecture: Adopt a multiregion strategy by deploying AKS clusters deployed across different Azure regions to maximize availability and provide business continuity.
before.description: Internet facing workloads should leverage Azure Front Door or Azure Traffic Manager to route traffic globally across AKS clusters.

before.name: wafsg-ManyAdvancedDeploymentPatternsReleaseEngineeringProcess
before.title: Workload architecture: Use platform capabilities in your release engineering process.
before.description: Kubernetes and ingress controllers support many advanced deployment patterns for inclusion in your release engineering process. Consider patterns like blue-green deployments or canary releases.

before.name: wafsg-NecessaryClusterWideConfigurationsClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Build an automated process to ensure your clusters are bootstrapped with the necessary cluster-wide configurations and deployments. This is often performed using GitOps.

before.name: wafsg-ReadinessStatusesWorkloadArchitecture
before.title: Workload architecture: The workload should be designed to emit telemetry that can be collected, which should also include liveliness and readiness statuses.

before.name: wafsg-SeamlessOnboardingExperienceReferenceConfigureScraping
before.title: Workload architecture: Configure scraping of Prometheus metrics with Container insights.
before.description: Container insights, which are part of Azure Monitor, provide a seamless onboarding experience to collect Prometheus metrics. Reference Configure scraping of Prometheus metrics for more information.

before.name: wafsg-SourceCodeRepoClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use a template-based deployment using Bicep, Terraform, or others. Make sure that all deployments are repeatable, traceable, and stored in a source code repo.

before.name: wafsg-StampLevelBlueGreenDeploymentsMissionCriticalDesignAreas
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: For mission-critical workloads, use stamp-level blue/green deployments.
before.description: Automate your mission-critical design areas, including deployment and testing.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitectureApplicationPerformance
before.title: Workload architecture: Monitor application performance with Azure Monitor.
before.description: Configure Application Insights for code-based monitoring of applications running in an AKS cluster.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitectureContainer
before.title: Workload architecture: Optimize your workload to operate and deploy efficiently in a container.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitecturesContainerInsights-1-2
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Configure monitoring of cluster with Container insights.
before.description: Container insights help monitor the performance of containers by collecting memory and processor metrics from controllers, nodes, and containers that are available in Kubernetes through the Metrics API and container logs.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitecturesContainerInsights-1
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Enable Container insights to collect metrics, logs, and diagnostics to monitor the availability and performance of the cluster and workloads running on it.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitecturesWorkloadGovernance
before.title: Cluster and workload architectures: Enforce cluster and workload governance using Azure Policy.

before.name: revcl-LeverageAzureDevopsLogicAppCode
before.title: Leverage Azure DevOps or GitHub to streamline CI/CD and safeguard your Logic App code

before.name: revcl-AzureMonitorAlertsOperationalAlerts
before.title: Use Azure Monitor alerts for the generation of operational alerts.

before.name: revcl-AzureMonitorLogsInsights
before.title: Use Azure Monitor Logs for insights and reporting.

before.name: revcl-LogAnalyticsWorkspaceAzureAutomationAccounts
before.title: When using Change and Inventory Tracking via Azure Automation Accounts, ensure that you have selected supported regions for linking your Log Analytics workspace and automation accounts together.

before.name: revcl-LogRetentionRequirementsAzureStorage
before.title: Export logs to Azure Storage if your log retention requirements exceed twelve years. Use immutable storage with a write-once, read-many policy to make data non-erasable and non-modifiable for a user-specified interval.

before.name: revcl-SingleMonitorLogsWorkspaceAzureRoleBasedAccessControl
before.title: Use a single monitor logs workspace to manage platforms centrally except where Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC), data sovereignty requirements, or data retention policies mandate separate workspaces.

before.name: revcl-VirtualMachinesUserPasswordsKeyVaultSecrets
before.title: Use Key Vault secrets to avoid hard-coding sensitive information such as credentials (virtual machines user passwords), certificates or keys.

before.name: wafsg-CuratedEnvironmentsMachineLearning
before.title: Simplicity: Use curated environments optimized for Machine Learning, when available.

before.name: wafsg-CurateModelTrainingEnvironmentsUnnecessaryImageBuilds
before.title: Curate model training environments: Use curated environments optimized for Machine Learning, when available.
before.description: Curated environments are pre-created environments provided by Machine Learning that speed up deployment time and reduce deployment and training latency. Using curated environments improves training and deployment success rates and avoids unnecessary image builds. Curated environments, such as Azure Container for PyTorch, can also be optimized for training large models on Machine Learning.

before.name: wafsg-DeployedModelsDataDrift
before.title: Observability: Monitor the performance of your deployed models including data drift.

before.name: wafsg-DifferentPerformantSkusOnlineEndpoints
before.title: Monitor infrastructure: If your models are deployed to online endpoints, enable Application Insights to monitor online endpoints and deployments.Monitor training infrastructure to ensure you're meeting your baseline requirements.Ensure you're collecting resource logs for Machine Learning.
before.description: Monitoring endpoints gives you visibility into metrics such as request latency and requests per minute. You can compare your performance versus your baseline and use this information to make changes to compute resources accordingly. Monitoring metrics such as network bytes can alert you if you're approaching quota limits and prevent throttling.Likewise, monitoring your training environment provides you with the information to make changes to your training environment. Use that information to decide to scale in or out, scale up or down with different performant SKUs, or choose between CPUs or GPUs.

before.name: wafsg-FineTunePretrainedFoundationalMachineLearningModelsMachineLearningModelCatalogs
before.title: Take advantage of model catalogs and registries: Take advantage of Machine Learning model catalogs and registries to store, version, and share machine learning assets.Use Machine Learning model catalogs to help you implement A/B testing and deployment of models.
before.description: Use Machine Learning model registries to store and version your machine learning models to track changes and maintain lineage with the job and datasets used for training. With Machine Learning model catalogs, your data science teams can discover, evaluate, and fine tune pretrained foundational machine learning models. Storing versioned models in Machine Learning model registries supports deployment strategies such as A/B releases, canary releases, and rollbacks.

before.name: wafsg-GoodMachineLearningOperationsMlopsPractices
before.title: Automate for efficiency: Follow good machine learning operations (MLOps) practices. When possible, build end-to-end automated pipelines for data preparation, training, and scoring processes. In development, use scripts instead of notebooks for training models, as scripts are easier to integrate into automated pipelines.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningModelCatalogsMachineLearningAssets
before.title: Development standards: Take advantage of Machine Learning model catalogs and registries to store, version, and share machine learning assets.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspaceInstancesMultipleSeparateWorkspaces
before.title: Minimize Machine Learning workspace instances: Minimize the number of workspaces, when possible, to reduce maintenance.
before.description: Limiting the number of workspaces reduces the maintenance effort and cost of operation. For requirements, such as security, you might need multiple separate workspaces. Minimize the number of workspaces when possible.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspacesOtherDeploymentEnvironments
before.title: Deploy with confidence: Implement infrastructure as code (IaC) for Machine Learning workspaces, compute clusters, compute instances, and other deployment environments.

before.name: wafsg-MonitoringDataDriftInputData
before.title: Monitor model performance: Monitor the performance of your deployed models, and detect data drift on datasets.
before.description: Monitoring deployed models ensures your models meet the performance requirements.Monitoring data drift helps you detect changes in the input data that can lead to a decline in your model’s performance. Managing data drift helps you ensure that your model provides accurate results over time.

before.name: wafsg-OnlineEndpointsApplicationInsights
before.title: Observability: If your models are deployed to online endpoints, enable Application Insights to monitor online endpoints and deployments. Monitor training infrastructure to ensure you're meeting your baseline requirements.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafConfigurationNewRuleSetVersion
before.title: Define your Azure Application Gateway WAF configuration as code. By using code, you can more easily adopt new rule set version and gain additional protection.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafLogsDiagnosticSettings
before.title: Add diagnostic settings to save your Azure Application Gateway WAF logs.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafLogsMicrosoftSentinel
before.title: Send Azure Application Gateway WAF logs to Microsoft Sentinel.

before.name: revcl-CustomErrorPagesPersonalizedUserExperience
before.title: Create custom error pages to display a personalized user experience

before.name: revcl-GatewayManagedCookiesUserSession
before.title: Use gateway-managed cookies to direct traffic from a user session to the same server for processing

before.name: revcl-LegacyWafConfigurationWafPolicies
before.title: Use WAF Policies instead of the legacy WAF configuration.

before.name: wafsg-ApplicationGatewayHighTrafficSupportApplicationGatewayCapacity
before.title: Monitor capacity metrics
before.description: Use these metrics as indicators of utilization of the provisioned Application Gateway capacity. We strongly recommend setting up alerts on capacity. For details, see Application Gateway high traffic support.

before.name: wafsg-AzureMonitorNetworkInsightsNetworkResources
before.title: Use Azure Monitor Network Insights
before.description: Azure Monitor Network Insights provides a comprehensive view of health and metrics for network resources, including Application Gateway. For additional details and supported capabilities for Application Gateway, see Azure Monitor Network insights.

before.name: wafsg-DataPlaneRelatedProblemsIncorrectKeyVaultConfiguration
before.title: Monitor Key Vault configuration issues using Azure Advisor
before.description: Application Gateway checks for the renewed certificate version in the linked Key Vault at every 4-hour interval. If it is inaccessible due to any incorrect Key Vault configuration, it logs that error and pushes a corresponding Advisor recommendation. You must configure the Advisor alerts to stay updated and fix such issues immediately to avoid any Control or Data plane related problems. For more information, see Investigating and resolving key vault errors. To set an alert for this specific case, use the Recommendation Type as Resolve Azure Key Vault issue for your Application Gateway.

before.name: wafsg-LoadBalancerTcpResetMatchTimeoutSettings
before.title: Match timeout settings with the backend application
before.description: Ensure you have configured the IdleTimeout settings to match the listener and traffic characteristics of the backend application. The default value is set to four minutes and can be configured to a maximum of 30. For more information, see Load Balancer TCP Reset and Idle Timeout.For workload considerations, see Monitoring application health for reliability.

before.name: wafsg-MatchTimeoutSettingsBackendApplication
before.title: Match timeout settings with the backend application

before.name: wafsg-SameVirtualNetworkSnatPortLimitations
before.title: Consider SNAT port limitations in your design
before.description: SNAT port limitations are important for backend connections on the Application Gateway. There are separate factors that affect how Application Gateway reaches the SNAT port limit. For example, if the backend is a public IP address, it will require its own SNAT port. In order to avoid SNAT port limitations, you can increase the number of instances per Application Gateway, scale out the backends to have more IP addresses, or move your backends into the same virtual network and use private IP addresses for the backends.Requests per second (RPS) on the Application Gateway will be affected if the SNAT port limit is reached. For example, if an Application Gateway reaches the SNAT port limit, then it won't be able to open a new connection to the backend, and the request will fail.

before.name: wafsg-SnatPortLimitations
before.title: Configure and monitor SNAT port limitations

before.name: wafsg-UnhealthyHostCountResponseStatusBackendLastByteResponseTime
before.title: Troubleshoot using metrics
before.description: There are other metrics that can indicate issues either at Application Gateway or the backend. We recommend evaluating the following alerts:- Unhealthy Host Count- Response Status (dimension 4xx and 5xx)- Backend Response Status (dimension 4xx and 5xx)- Backend Last Byte Response Time- Application Gateway Total TimeFor more information, see Metrics for Application Gateway.

before.name: wafsg-WebApplicationFirewallApplicationGatewayInstances
before.title: Enable diagnostics on Application Gateway and Web Application Firewall (WAF)
before.description: Diagnostic logs allow you to view firewall logs, performance logs, and access logs. Use these logs to manage and troubleshoot issues with Application Gateway instances. For more information, see Back-end health and diagnostic logs for Application Gateway.

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallAzureMonitor
before.title: Integrate Azure Firewall with Azure Monitor and enable diagnostic logging to store and analyze firewall logs.

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallClassicRulesFirewallPolicy
before.title: Migrate from Azure Firewall Classic rules (if exist) to Firewall Policy.

before.name: revcl-FirewallRulesBackups
before.title: Implement backups for your firewall rules

before.name: revcl-ResourceSpecificDestinationTableAzureFirewallDeployments
before.title: Add diagnostic settings to save logs, using the Resource Specific destination table, for all Azure Firewall deployments.

before.name: wafsg-AzfwLatencyProbeMetricsAzureFirewallCapacity
before.title: Monitor key metrics and create alerts for indicators of the utilization of Azure Firewall capacity.
before.description: Alerts should be created to monitor at least Throughput, Firewall health state, SNAT port utilization and AZFW Latency Probe metrics.For information about monitoring logs and metrics, see Monitor Azure Firewall logs and metrics.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallConfigurationInventory
before.title: Maintain inventory and backup of Azure Firewall configuration and Policies.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallMicrosoftDefender
before.title: Integrate Azure Firewall with Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallPortalExperienceAzureFirewallMonitoringWorkbook
before.title: Use the built-in Azure Firewall Monitoring Workbook.
before.description: Azure Firewall portal experience now includes a new workbook under the Monitoring section UI, a separate installation is no more required. With the Azure Firewall Workbook, you can extract valuable insights from Azure Firewall events, delve into your application and network rules, and examine statistics regarding firewall activities across URLs, ports, and addresses.

before.name: wafsg-ExternalLogicAppAzurePolicyArtifacts
before.title: Maintain regular backups of Azure Policy artifacts.
before.description: If Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) approach is used to maintain Azure Firewall and all dependencies then backup and versioning of Azure Firewall Policies should be already in place. If not, a companion mechanism based on external Logic App can be deployed to automate and provide an effective solution.

before.name: wafsg-IpGroupsUsageRecommendationRuleProcessingPerformance
before.title: Regularly review Policy Analytics dashboard to identify potential issues.
before.description: Policy Analytics is a new feature that provides insights into the impact of your Azure Firewall policies. It helps you identify potential issues (hitting policy limits, low utilization rules, redundant rules, rules too generic, IP Groups usage recommendation) in your policies and provides recommendations to improve your security posture and rule processing performance.

before.name: wafsg-KustoQueryLanguageQueriesAzureFirewallLogs
before.title: Become familiar with KQL (Kusto Query Language) queries to allow quick analysis and troubleshooting using Azure Firewall logs.
before.description: Sample queries are provided for Azure Firewall. Those will enable you to quickly identify what's happening inside your firewall and check to see which rule was triggered, or which rule is allowing/blocking a request.

before.name: wafsg-LeverageDiagnosticLogsFirewallMonitoring
before.title: Leverage diagnostic logs for firewall monitoring and troubleshooting.

before.name: wafsg-ManyMonitoringToolsAzureFirewallResources
before.title: Enable Diagnostic Logs for Azure Firewall.
before.description: Diagnostic Logs is a key component for many monitoring tools and strategies for Azure Firewall and should be enabled. You can monitor Azure Firewall by using firewall logs or workbooks. You can also use activity logs for auditing operations on Azure Firewall resources.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftSentinelSolutionsAzureNetworkSecurity
before.title: Configure Azure Firewall integration with Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel.
before.description: If these tools are available in the environment, it is recommended to leverage integration with Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel solutions. With Microsoft Defender for Cloud integration, you can visualize the all-up status of network infrastructure and network security in one place, including Azure Network Security across all VNets and Virtual Hubs spread across different regions in Azure. Integration with Microsoft Sentinel provides threat detection and prevention capabilities.

before.name: wafsg-NetworkSecurityGroupsIntraVnetTrafficControl
before.title: Do not use Azure Firewall for intra-VNet traffic control.
before.description: Azure Firewall should be used to control traffic across VNets, between VNets and on-premises networks, outbound traffic to the Internet and incoming non-HTTP/s traffic. For intra-VNet traffic control, it is recommended to use Network Security Groups.

before.name: wafsg-PolicyInsightsAnalytics
before.title: Regularly review your Policy insights and analytics.

before.name: wafsg-PreviousDiagnosticLogsFormatStructuredFirewallLogsFormat
before.title: Use Structured Firewall Logs format.
before.description: Structured Firewall Logs are a type of log data that are organized in a specific new format. They use a predefined schema to structure log data in a way that makes it easy to search, filter, and analyze. The latest monitoring tools are based on this type of logs hence it is often a pre-requisite. Use the previous Diagnostic Logs format only if there is an existing tool with a pre-requisite on that. Do not enable both logging formats at the same time.

before.name: revcl-AzureDnsDnsRecords
before.title: Enable auto-registration for Azure DNS to automatically manage the lifecycle of the DNS records for the virtual machines deployed within a virtual network.

before.name: revcl-AzurePrivateDnsDelegatedZone
before.title: For environments where name resolution in Azure is all that's required, use Azure Private DNS for resolution with a delegated zone for name resolution (such as 'azure.contoso.com').

before.name: revcl-RedHatOpenshiftPreferredDnsSolution
before.title: Special workloads that require and deploy their own DNS (such as Red Hat OpenShift) should use their preferred DNS solution.

before.name: revcl-ConnectionMonitorConnectivityMonitoring
before.title: Use Connection Monitor for connectivity monitoring across the network, especially between on-premises and Azure.

before.name: revcl-ExpressRouteInsightsExpressrouteAvailability
before.title: Monitor ExpressRoute availability and utilization using built-in Express Route Insights.

before.name: revcl-ExpressrouteVirtualNetworkGatewayDiagnosticLogs
before.title: Configure diagnostic logs and alerts for ExpressRoute virtual network gateway.

before.name: wafsg-ConnectionMonitoringAzureNetwork
before.title: Configure connection monitoring between your on-premises and Azure network.

before.name: wafsg-ExpressrouteGatewayConnectionsExpressrouteResourceMetrics
before.title: Review ExpressRoute resource metrics
before.description: ExpressRoute uses Azure Monitor to collect metrics and create alerts base on your configuration. Metrics are collected for ExpressRoute circuits, ExpressRoute gateways, ExpressRoute gateway connections, and ExpressRoute Direct. These metrics are useful for diagnosing connectivity problems and understanding the performance of your ExpressRoute connection.

before.name: wafsg-ExpressrouteInsightsNetworkInsights
before.title: Review metrics and dashboards available through ExpressRoute Insights using Network Insights.

before.name: wafsg-ExpressroutePrivatePeeringMicrosoftPeeringConnection
before.title: Configure connection monitoring
before.description: Connection monitoring allows you to monitor connectivity between your on-premises resources and Azure over the ExpressRoute private peering and Microsoft peering connection. Connection monitor can detect networking issues by identifying where along the network path the problem is and help you quickly resolve configuration or hardware failures.

before.name: wafsg-HealthNotificationsUpcomingMaintenance
before.title: Configure Service Health
before.description: Set up Service Health notifications to alert when planned and upcoming maintenance is happening to all ExpressRoute circuits in your subscription. Service Health also displays past maintenance along with RCA if an unplanned maintenance were to occur.

before.name: wafsg-ServiceHealthNotification
before.title: Configure Service Health for receiving notification.

before.name: wafsg-ThroughputGatewayMetricsNetworkInsights
before.title: Review metrics with Network Insights
before.description: ExpressRoute Insights with Network Insights allow you to review and analyze ExpressRoute circuits, gateways, connections metrics and health dashboards. ExpressRoute Insights also provide a topology view of your ExpressRoute connections where you can view details of your peering components all in a single place.Metrics available:- Availability- Throughput- Gateway metrics

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafConfigurationNewRuleSetVersion
before.title: Define your Azure Front Door WAF configuration as code. By using code, you can more easily adopt new rule set version and gain additional protection.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafLogsDiagnosticSettings
before.title: Add diagnostic settings to save your Azure Front Door WAF logs.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafLogsMicrosoftSentinel
before.title: Send Azure Front Door WAF logs to Microsoft Sentinel.

before.name: revcl-CustomerManagedTlsCertificatesAzureFrontDoor
before.title: If you use customer-managed TLS certificates with Azure Front Door, use the 'Latest' certificate version. Reduce the risk of outages caused by manual certificate renewal

before.name: revcl-ManagedTlsCertificatesAzureFrontDoor
before.title: Use managed TLS certificates with Azure Front Door. Reduce operational cost and risk of outages due to certificate renewals.

queries.arg: cdnresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.cdn/profiles/customdomains' | extend frontDoorId = substring(id, 0, indexof(id, '/customdomains')) | extend compliant = (isnull(properties['tlsSettings']['certificateType']) or tolower(properties['tlsSettings']['certificateType']) =~ 'customercertificate') | project compliant, id = frontDoorId

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorConfigurationCriticalOperationalIssues
before.title: Capture logs and metrics.  Include resource activity logs, access logs, health probe logs, and WAF logs. Set up alerts.
before.description: Monitoring ingress flow is a crucial part of monitoring an application. You want to track requests and make performance and security improvements. You need data to debug your Azure Front Door configuration.  With alerts in place, you can get instant notifications of any critical operational issues.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorForwardCompatibility
before.title: Use HTTP to HTTPS redirection to support forward compatibility.
before.description: When redirection is enabled, Azure Front Door automatically redirects clients that are using older protocol to use HTTPS for a secure experience.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorManagedTlsCertificates
before.title: Use managed TLS certificates when possible.
before.description: Azure Front Door can issue and manage certificates for you. This feature eliminates the need for certificate renewals and minimizes the risk of an outage due to an invalid or expired TLS certificate.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorProfileAnalyticsReports
before.title: Review the built-in analytics reports.
before.description: A holistic view of your Azure Front Door profile helps drive improvements based on traffic and security reports through WAF metrics.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorRedirectionCapabilities
before.title: Simplify configurations. Use Azure Front Door to easily manage configurations. For example, suppose your architecture supports microservices. Azure Front Door supports redirection capabilities, so you can use path-based redirection to target individual services.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFrontDoorRoutingMethodsWeightedLoadBalancingApproach
before.title: Handle progressive exposure by using Azure Front Door routing methods. For a weighted load balancing approach you can use a canary deployment to send a specific percentage of traffic to a back end. This approach helps you test new features and releases in a controlled environment before you roll them out.

before.name: wafsg-AzureResourceManagerTemplatesAzureFrontDoorInstance
before.title: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) technologies. Use IaC technologies like Bicep and Azure Resource Manager templates to provision the Azure Front Door instance. These declarative approaches provide consistency and straightforward maintenance. For example, by using IaC technologies, you can easily adopt new ruleset versions.

before.name: wafsg-CertificateManagementOperationalBurden
before.title: Offload certificate management to Azure. Ease the operational burden associated with certification rotation and renewals.

before.name: wafsg-RelevantAzureFrontDoorLogsAzureFrontDoorOperationalData
before.title: Collect and analyze Azure Front Door operational data as part of your workload monitoring. Capture relevant Azure Front Door logs and metrics with Azure Monitor Logs. This data helps you troubleshoot, understand user behaviors, and optimize operations.

before.name: wafsg-WildcardTlsCertificatesConfiguration
before.title: Use wildcard TLS certificates.
before.description: You don't need to modify the configuration to add or specify each subdomain separately.

before.name: revcl-ApplicationDeliveryServicesAzureFrontDoor-1
before.title: Send WAF logs from your application delivery services like Azure Front Door and Azure Application Gateway to Microsoft Sentinel. Detect attacks and integrate WAF telemetry into your overall Azure environment.

before.name: revcl-ApplicationDeliveryServicesAzureFrontDoor
before.title: Add diagnostic settings to save WAF logs from application delivery services like Azure Front Door and Azure Application Gateway. Regularly review the logs to check for attacks and for false positive detections.

before.name: revcl-NetworkWatcherTrafficFlows
before.title: Use Network Watcher to proactively monitor traffic flows

before.name: revcl-AzureMonitorEndState
before.title: Use Azure Monitor for Networks to monitor the end-to-end state of the networks on Azure.

before.name: revcl-AzureMonitorInsightsVirtualWan
before.title: Use Azure Monitor Insights for Virtual WAN to monitor the end-to-end topology of the Virtual WAN, status, and key metrics.

before.name: revcl-SimplifiedAzureNetworkingManagementVirtualWanRoutingDesigns
before.title: Consider Virtual WAN for simplified Azure networking management, and make sure your scenario is explicitly described in the list of Virtual WAN routing designs

before.name: revcl-AzureCompatibleRdPartyBackupSolutionAzureNativeBackupCapabilities
before.title: Use Azure-native backup capabilities, or an Azure-compatible, 3rd-party backup solution.

before.name: wafsg-AzureMonitorLogsWorkspaceStorageInsightsDashboards
before.title: Monitor the health of your storage account: Create Storage insights dashboards to monitor availability, performance, and resilience metrics. Set up alerts to identify and address problems in your system before your customers notice them. Use diagnostic settings to route resource logs to an Azure Monitor Logs workspace. Then you can query logs to investigate alerts more deeply.

before.name: wafsg-AzureResourceManagerTemplatesExistingDevopsProcesses
before.title: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to define the details of your storage accounts in Azure Resource Manager templates (ARM templates), Bicep, or Terraform.
before.description: You can use your existing DevOps processes to deploy new storage accounts, and use Azure Policy to enforce their configuration.

before.name: wafsg-BlobInventoryReportsCostEfficientAccessTiers
before.title: Set up policies that delete blobs or move them to cost-efficient access tiers: Create a lifecycle management policy with an initial set of conditions. Policy runs automatically delete or set the access tier of blobs based on the conditions you define. Periodically analyze container use by using Monitor metrics and blob inventory reports so that you can refine conditions to optimize cost efficiency.

before.name: wafsg-EmergencyRecoveryPlansDataProtectionFeatures
before.title: Create maintenance and emergency recovery plans: Consider data protection features, backup and restore operations, and failover procedures. Prepare for potential data loss and data inconsistencies and the time and cost of failing over.

before.name: wafsg-FileSharesUseMonitor
before.title: Use Monitor to analyze metrics, such as availability, latency, and usage, and to create alerts.
before.description: Monitor provides a view of availability, performance, and resiliency for your file shares.

before.name: wafsg-StandardFileSharesDifferentAccessTier
before.title: Periodically review file share activity: Share activity can change over time. Move standard file shares to cooler access tiers, or you can provision or deprovision capacity for premium shares. When you move standard file shares to a different access tier, you incur a transaction charge. Move standard file shares only when needed to reduce your monthly bill.

before.name: wafsg-StorageAccountContentsAzureSynapseAnalytics
before.title: Enable blob inventory reports: Enable blob inventory reports to review the retention, legal hold, or encryption status of your storage account contents. You can also use blob inventory reports to understand the total data size, age, tier distribution, or other attributes of your data. Use tools such as Azure Databricks or Azure Synapse Analytics and Power BI to better visualize inventory data and to create reports for stakeholders.

before.name: wafsg-StorageInsightsUnifiedView
before.title: Use Storage insights to track the health and performance of your storage accounts. Storage insights provides a unified view of the failures, performance, availability, and capacity for all your storage accounts.
before.description: You can track the health and operation of each of your accounts. Easily create dashboards and reports that stakeholders can use to track the health of your storage accounts.

before.name: revcl-LeverageAzureDevopsFunctionAppCode
before.title: Leverage Azure DevOps or GitHub to streamline CI/CD and safeguard your Function App code

before.name: revcl-LeverageAzureDevopsLogicAppCode-1
before.title: Leverage Azure DevOps or GitHub to streamline CI/CD and safeguard your Logic App code

before.name: wafsg-AppServicePlanAppChanges
before.title: (App Service plan) Validate app changes in the staging slot before you swap it with the production slot.
before.description: Avoid downtime and errors.  Quickly revert to the last-known good state if you detect a problem after a swap.

before.name: wafsg-AppServiceResourceProviderCertificationManagement
before.title: (App Service) Take advantage of App Service managed certificates to offload certification management to Azure.
before.description: App Service automatically handles processes like certificate procurement, certificate verification, certificate renewal, and importing certificates from Key Vault. Alternatively, upload your certificate to Key Vault and authorize the App Service resource provider to access it.

before.name: wafsg-AppServiceWebAppDeploymentStampsPattern
before.title: Deploy immutable units: Implement the Deployment Stamps pattern to compartmentalize App Service into an immutable stamp. App Service supports the use of containers, which are inherently immutable. Consider custom containers for your App Service web app.

before.name: wafsg-AzureLoadTestingAutomatedTests
before.title: Run automated tests: Before you promote a release of your web app, thoroughly test its performance, functionality, and integration with other components. Use Azure Load Testing, which integrates with Apache JMeter, a popular tool for performance testing. Explore automated tools for other types of testing, such as Phantom for functional testing.

before.name: wafsg-CustomDomainsTlsCertificates
before.title: Manage certificates: For custom domains, you need to manage TLS certificates.

before.name: wafsg-FrequentLoggingStorageCosts
before.title: (App Service) Enable diagnostics logs for the application and the instance.  Frequent logging can slow down the performance of the system, add to storage costs, and introduce risk if you have unsecure access to logs. Follow these best practices:  - Log the right level of information.  - Set retention policies.  - Keep an audit trail of authorized access and unauthorized attempts. - Treat logs as data and apply data-protection controls.
before.description: Diagnostic logs provide valuable insights into your app's behavior. Monitor traffic patterns and identify anomalies.

before.name: wafsg-InstanceHealthProbesHealthProbeRequests
before.title: (App Service) Monitor the health of your instances and activate instance health probes. Set up a specific path for handling health probe requests.
before.description: You can detect problems promptly and take necessary actions to maintain availability and performance.

before.name: wafsg-SameVirtualMachineDeploymentSlots
before.title: Manage releases: Use deployment slots to manage releases effectively. You can deploy your application to a slot, perform testing, and validate its functionality. After verification, you can seamlessly move the app to production. This process doesn't incur extra costs because the slot runs in the same virtual machine (VM) environment as the production instance.

before.name: wafsg-SeparateAppServicePlansSeparateInstances
before.title: Keep production environments safe: Create separate App Service plans to run production and pre-production environments. Don't make changes directly in the production environment to ensure stability and reliability. Separate instances allow flexibility in development and testing before you promote changes to production.
